claims.claim: 6x256 per byte + structured whole-field values, 1603 cases

n3_sample_read.tail.label: untested
n3_sample_read.tail.note: 48-bit field swept per byte (6x256) plus structured whole-field values. Bytes 1-5 are FULLY INERT (256/256 each); only byte 0 matters, where 53 values fault with 'Caused GPU Hang Error'. Intra-run 1603/1603 stable; 12 cross-run misses are load-related. | WITHHELD 2026-08-30 on EXP-0192, the PRE-REGISTERED successor to EXP-0191's post-hoc finding. `audit.py`'s `sig_of()` gives `ok` and `fault` different signatures, so `moved` COUNTS A FAULT AS MOVEMENT. This row is **Case C: fewer than two distinct VALID payloads (V=1) but 1522 LEGAL values** -- multiple values ran legally and were INDISTINGUISHABLE. That is an inertness observation which the fault signature re-scored as movement; absent the defect it would have been INERT-SINGLE, already in the WITHHOLD set. Cross-run agreement is 100% and does not help: `moved` is precisely the ok/fault transition count, and a perfectly reproducible fault wall is a perfectly reproducible HAZARD MAP, not a semantic. The fault wall remains a first-class fact and a real legal-set bound. Case C says the PROMOTION is unsupported, not that the field is inert -- a single valid payload can also mean the arm lacked detection power.

pixel_order.flags.label: hardware-run
pixel_order.flags.note: ACQUIRE: correct iff bit0==0 AND (v & 0x0e)!=0 (112/256). RELEASE: correct iff (v & 0x0f)>=2 (224/256). byte+4 is therefore a REAL field with a large legal set, NOT the constant 0x06 that db.json's match clause pins it to - see db_defects.

claims.claim: ACQUIRE bit4==1 AND (bit6 XOR bit7)==1, 64/256, baseline 0x50

pixel_order.scope.label: hardware-run
pixel_order.scope.note: ACQUIRE member: correct iff bit4==1 AND (bit6 XOR bit7)==1 (64/256, baseline 0x50). RELEASE member: correct iff bit4==1 AND bit7==1 (64/256, baseline 0xd0). Low nibble don't-care in both. This settles db.json's open note 'scope {0x50,0xd0}, bit7 differs' with the full accepted set.

vtx_coord_xform.mode.label: hardware-run
vtx_coord_xform.mode.note: Correct exactly when (mode & 0xf3) in {0x22,0xe2} (8/256, baseline 0x22). 240 of 256 values SUPPRESS THE DRAW ENTIRELY (no_draw, confirmed twice with a healthy device in between); 8 give a wrong pixel.

Intra-run 1339/1339 stable. | WITHHELD 2026-08-30 by EXP-0193, applying EXP-0192's UNCHANGED pre-registered criterion to the full 337-arm STABLE-LIVE population. **Case C: 1 distinct VALID payload(s) across 817 LEGAL values** -- values ran legally and were indistinguishable. `moved_total` equals the hard-class cell count EXACTLY, and cross-run agreement is 100%: a perfectly reproducible hazard map, not a semantic.
